guitar.modelsText: Gibson Flying V (black and white 'Boogie Body' V)
models: Gibson Flying V (black and white 'Boogie Body' V)
guitar.evidence: Michael Schenker is one of the most iconic Flying V players in rock history, with his black-and-white V being his signature look, well documented.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown with high confidence given the genuinely iconic, well-documented instrument.

tone.target: bright mid-gain Marshall crunch with lead sustain
tone.profile: bright mid-gain Marshall crunch with lead sustain
tone.summary: A tight, bright signal chain utilizing a light OD boost for grit, followed by the UK 45 amp model to achieve the characteristic Plexi-style mid-gain crunch, finished with chorus and delay for dimension.
corrections: favor Marshall crunch over generic rock

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide light grit and upper-mid bite boost without sounding like a full overdrive.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate the 'light OD boost' clue, focusing on mid-range enhancement rather than heavy saturation.

alternatives.reason: A slightly more aggressive option if more grit is needed.

blocks.purpose: Bypass or use a subtle gain stage if needed; the Green OD handles most of the required crunch.
blocks.gap: No dedicated distortion unit is strictly necessary as the UK 45 amp model provides sufficient mid-gain saturation. Keeping it bypassed for clarity.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the classic Marshall/Plexi sound required for hard rock crunch and upper-mid bite.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative if the tone needs slightly more punch.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required classic Marshall cabinet tone and frequency response.
Add dimension and width to the lead lines for a more 'singing' sustain effect.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used as an enhancement tool, not essential, but helps achieve the desired dimensionality.

blocks.purpose: Add depth and space to the lead sustain, enhancing the classic hard rock feel.
blocks.gap: A moderate delay is used to enhance the 'singing' quality of the sustained notes without cluttering the mix.

blocks.purpose: Provide subtle natural ambience to round out the tone and give a sense of space.
blocks.gap: A light Room reverb is preferred over Plate/Spring to maintain the dry, punchy feel of classic hard rock while adding necessary depth.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the vintage Marshall/Plexi character.

proposals.reason: Enhance upper-mid bite and vintage Plexi realism.
